findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime fields
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` after `value = getattr(item, self.key)`. The endpoint wires this paginator in with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `self.key` is `"datetime"` and `getattr(item, "datetime")` returns a `datetime.datetime` object. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: a float is required`, so every call through the new path (including the very first request, because `build_cursor` calls `key(...)` to seed the next/prev cursor) will raise 500. The optimized paginator should subclass `DateTimePaginator`'s key conversion (multiplier + strftime) or be otherwise datetime-aware.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing crashes Django QuerySet
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, the advanced-features branch sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (which can be negative) and then does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly disallows negative indices and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` (or the equivalent TypeError on newer Django). The "negative offset support" advertised by the new class therefore crashes the request whenever a client sends a cursor with a negative offset. There is no defensive clamp (`max(0, ...)`) and no fallback, so the feature is non-functional in practice.

findings.title: BasePaginator.get_result now passes negative offsets to QuerySet slicing
findings.body: The new line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` deliberately lets a negative `offset` flow into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when the cursor is a prev cursor. Cursor offsets are parsed straight from the URL via `int(bits[1])` in `Cursor.from_string`, so any client (or buggy prior response) that produces a negative offset will now hit Django's negative-indexing AssertionError. The accompanying comment ("This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is factually wrong: Django does NOT handle negative slicing and the previous code did not claim to. This change advertises a behavior that does not work.

findings.title: Comment falsely claims QuerySet handles negative offsets
findings.body: The comment block above the new offset calculation says "This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions." Django's QuerySet raises on negative slicing (see the related finding at line 182/882). The comment is misleading and should either be removed or replaced with a real explanation of the intent plus a real guard, e.g. clamping to `>= 0` like the not-is_prev branch.

findings.title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination path
findings.body: The PR introduces a new request gate (`optimized_pagination=true`) and a new paginator class but does not add any tests for the new code path in `organization_auditlogs.py` or `paginator.py`. Given that the new path currently 500s on any non-trivial cursor (see other findings), tests would have caught the regression. At minimum, a test should cover (a) that `optimized_pagination=true` for an admin uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and succeeds end-to-end on `order_by="-datetime"`, and (b) that bad/negative cursors do not crash the endpoint.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result without a real perf win
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result; the only behavioral difference is the negative-offset branch (which is itself broken — see other findings). The endpoint always passes `enable_advanced_features=True` when it opts in, so the flag is effectively dead. There is no documented or measurable performance improvement over DateTimePaginator/BasePaginator: the same queryset is built, sliced, and `build_cursor` is invoked identically. Either delete the class and the gating code, or implement the actual optimization (e.g. a keyset pagination scheme or a bounded lookup) and benchmark it.
